topic: Performance: 5 common reasons a web app feels slow
caption:
Is your web app slow? It's usually one of these 5 things. ⚡

1️⃣ Images that are far too big
2️⃣ Too many requests per screen
3️⃣ No caching
4️⃣ Database queries without indexes
5️⃣ Shipping too much JavaScript

The good news: most of these are fixable without a rebuild. Swipe for what to look at in each. →

App feeling sluggish? DM us SPEED and tell us where it slows down.

Save this for your next performance review. 🔖

slides.title:
5 reasons your
web app feels slow.
slides.sub: Most are fixable without a rebuild. Swipe →

slides.title: Images that are too big
slides.body: Serve resized, compressed, modern formats and lazy-load what's below the fold. Often the quickest win.

slides.title: Too many requests
slides.body: A screen that makes a dozen API calls waits on all of them. Combine or batch what loads together.

slides.title: No caching
slides.body: If data rarely changes, cache it in the browser, at a CDN or on the server instead of rebuilding it every time.

slides.title: Unindexed queries
slides.body: A query that's fast with 100 rows can crawl with a million. Add the right indexes as your data grows.

slides.title: Too much JavaScript
slides.body: Big bundles delay every page. Split code and render on the server where it helps, as Next.js makes easy.
